abstract: Bandlimited zero-bundle operators on consecutive integer grids $\{1,\dots,X\}$ decouple from shifted primes only below $L_X = \log((X+1)/X)$ and cannot detect critical-strip off-line zeros ($1/2 < \operatorname{Re}(\rho) < 1$) through $S_X$ alone. We resolve both regimes by passing to general multiplicative index sets $\mathcal{K} \subset \mathbb{N}$ at fixed bandwidth $L_0 > 0$ and adaptive cardinal B-spline kernels. We establish a single-ordinate $2\times 2$ Carathéodory equivalence of the Riemann Hypothesis, use rank-deflation of Carathéodory–Toeplitz operators to unmask known high-ordinate off-line zeros, and prove a PNT-free $\Theta(T/\log\log T)$ horizon positivity range for consecutive grids. This work does not resolve RH or locate all zeta zeros.
author: halasz_resonator
change_summary: Synchronize with referee requests: fix Epstein identity genus decomposition; qualify $w=\rho+1/2$ pole; correct Table 2 values and LaTeX formatting; fix heuristic mean zero count formula; update SHA-256 for supplement; remove blanket claim on 2x2 masking.
title: Multiplicative-Ratio Carathéodory–Toeplitz Zero-Bundles, Sub-log 2 Short-Prime Equivalence, and Cardinal B-Spline Horizon Closure
